title: Weakly augmented double diagrams and natural hammock maps
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with a wide subcategory $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three, with universes enlarged so all diagrams are small. Use the hammock localization of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] and simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $P:\Delta\to\mathcal C$ and $Q:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ have augmentation $p:P\to\operatorname{const}x$ and coaugmentation $i:\operatorname{const}y\to Q$, all of whose components belong to $W$. Define $I(P,Q)$ to have objects $(m,n,h:P^m\to Q_n)$ and morphisms $(\alpha:[m]\to[m'],\beta:[n']\to[n])$ satisfying $Q(\beta)h=h'P(\alpha)$. A chain of morphisms determines a commutative grid of zigzags $x\xleftarrow{p^m}P^m\xrightarrow{h}Q_n\xleftarrow{i_n}y$. Reducing this grid gives a simplicial map $\gamma_{P,Q}:NI(P,Q)\to L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x,y)$.

These maps are natural under a functor of such pairs $(\mathcal C,W)\to(\mathcal D,V)$ preserving the specified weak equivalences. They are also natural in the homotopy category of simplicial sets under natural transformations $a:P'\to P$, $b:Q\to Q'$ with weak-equivalence components and covering endpoint maps $c:x'\to x$, $d:y\to y'$: $pa=\operatorname{const}(c)p'$ and $bi=i'\operatorname{const}(d)$. Precisely, the map $NI(P,Q)\to NI(P',Q')$ given by $h\mapsto b_nha^m$ followed by $\gamma_{P',Q'}$ equals $\gamma_{P,Q}$ followed by hammock precomposition with $c$ and postcomposition with $d$, in that homotopy category. The comparisons are induced by inserting the commutative rows with vertical arrows $a,b$. No Reedy, lifting, cofibrancy, fibrancy or model-category hypotheses on $P,Q$ are required. No weak-equivalence assertion about $\gamma_{P,Q}$ is made.

source.place: Low, Revisiting function complexes and simplicial localisation, Lemma 3.4 and proof of Proposition 3.7(ii), printed pp.13–15; agent extension of the index-forgetting construction to weak augmentations, using the definition of hammocks in Hinich Section 1.2. No Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: Write composition in functional order. Identities in $I(P,Q)$ are $(1,1)$, and the composite of $(\alpha,\beta)$ followed by $(\alpha',\beta')$ is $(\alpha'\alpha,\beta\beta')$. Its required equality follows by substituting the two given equalities and using functoriality of $P,Q$. Thus this is a small category in the chosen universe. For each arrow of it, naturality of the augmentations gives $p^{m'}P(\alpha)=p^m$ and $Q(\beta)i_n=i_{n'}$. Since the two $p$-components and the two $i$-components are in $W$, two-out-of-three gives $P(\alpha),Q(\beta)\in W$. The same calculation applies to $P',Q'$ when these occur below.

source.place: Low, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7(ii), printed pp.12-15; agent extension using explicit padded rows, with only weak augmentations.

proof.text: Use the reduced hammocks and ordinary nerves of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. To a chain $t_0\to\cdots\to t_k$, with $t_j=(m_j,n_j,h_j)$, assign the $k+1$ rows $x\xleftarrow{p^{m_j}}P^{m_j}\xrightarrow{h_j}Q_{n_j}\xleftarrow{i_{n_j}}y$. The interior vertical arrows are $U_j=P(\alpha_j)$ and $V_j=Q(\beta_j)$ and the endpoint arrows are identities. The defining equality of $I$ gives the middle square; augmentation naturality gives the outer squares. Step 1 supplies the required vertical weak equivalences. Hence these are unreduced hammocks of word $-+-$. Reduction gives a simplicial map: [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation] identifies reduction with the natural maps from the fixed-word diagrams to the reduced mapping simplicial set. Deleting a row composes $U,V$, exactly as in the nerve; repeating a row inserts identities. This constructs $\gamma_{P,Q}$, including chains with identity columns or repeated vertices.

source.place: Low, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7(ii), printed pp.12-15; agent extension using explicit padded rows, with only weak augmentations.

proof.text: For a functor $F:(\mathcal C,W)\to(\mathcal D,V)$, send $(m,n,h)$ to $(m,n,Fh)$ and retain $(\alpha,\beta)$ on arrows. Applying $F$ to the defining commutative equation proves this is a functor $I(P,Q)\to I(FP,FQ)$. Applying $F$ entrywise to each grid in step 2 gives exactly its target grid. The reduction is natural for functors preserving the wide subcategories by [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation]; this includes functors that turn nonidentity arrows into identities. Thus the square involving $N I(F)$, the two $\gamma$ maps and the hammock functor commutes strictly. The hammock functor in [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] is the same entrywise functor.

source.place: Low, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7(ii), printed pp.12-15; agent extension using explicit padded rows, with only weak augmentations.

proof.text: Now fix $a,b,c,d$ as in the statement. The equation $p^m a^m=c p'^m$ and two-out-of-three imply $c\in W$; $b_n i_n=i'_n d$ similarly implies $d\in W$. On objects set $T(m,n,h)=(m,n,b_n h a^m)$ and keep $(\alpha,\beta)$ on arrows. Naturality of $a,b$ gives $Q'(\beta)b_n h a^m=b_{n'}Q(\beta)h a^m=b_{n'}h'P(\alpha)a^m=b_{n'}h'a^{m'}P'(\alpha)$, so $T:I(P,Q)\to I(P',Q')$ is a functor. Also $S(m,n,h)=(m,n,h a^m)$ defines $I(P,Q)\to I(P',Q)$. Write $K=N I(P,Q)$, and abbreviate $p_j=p^{m_j}$, $p'_j=p'^{m_j}$, $i_j=i_{n_j}$, $i'_j=i'_{n_j}$, $A_j=a^{m_j}$, $B_j=b_{n_j}$ and $U'_j=P'(\alpha_j)$, $V'_j=Q'(\beta_j)$.

source.place: Low, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7(ii), printed pp.12-15; agent extension using explicit padded rows, with only weak augmentations.

proof.text:
Construct $H_a:K\times\Delta^1\to L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x',y)$ using the hammock rule of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. Given a chain as in step 2 and a monotone $\theta:[k]\to[1]$, take row $j$ of word $+ - + -$ to be
$$x'\xrightarrow{1}x'\xleftarrow{p'_j}P'^{m_j}\xrightarrow{h_j A_j}Q_{n_j}\xleftarrow{i_j}y\quad(\theta(j)=0),$$
$$x'\xrightarrow{c}x\xleftarrow{p_j}P^{m_j}\xrightarrow{h_j}Q_{n_j}\xleftarrow{i_j}y\quad(\theta(j)=1).$$
For adjacent equal choices use the corresponding structure arrows; at a $0\to1$ change the three internal vertical arrows are $c$, $A_{j+1}U'_j=U_j A_j$, and $V_j$. All are in $W$. The squares commute by $pA=cp'$, naturality of $a$, and $V_jh_j=h_{j+1}U_j$. Endpoint vertical arrows are identities. These formulas respect composition and identities in the chain: for a skipped segment crossing the change, the $P$-column is $A_l U'_{j,l}=U_{j,l}A_j$ by naturality; the other columns compose by functoriality. Thus row restriction agrees with every simplicial operator. Reduce using [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation]. At $\theta=0$ deleting the first identity column gives $\gamma_{P',Q}NS$; at $\theta=1$ it gives $\gamma_{P,Q}$ precomposed in the hammock category with $c$.

source.place: Low, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7(ii), printed pp.12-15; agent extension using explicit padded rows, with only weak augmentations.

proof.text:
Construct $H_b:K\times\Delta^1\to L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x',y')$ with word $- + - +$. At row $j$ use
$$x'\xleftarrow{p'_j}P'^{m_j}\xrightarrow{h_j A_j}Q_{n_j}\xleftarrow{i_j}y\xrightarrow{d}y'\quad(\theta(j)=0),$$
$$x'\xleftarrow{p'_j}P'^{m_j}\xrightarrow{B_j h_j A_j}Q'_{n_j}\xleftarrow{i'_j}y'\xrightarrow{1}y'\quad(\theta(j)=1).$$
The same-choice vertical arrows are the structure arrows. At the change the internal vertical arrows are $U'_j$, $B_{j+1}V_j=V'_j B_j$, and $d$. These lie in $W$. The central square uses $V_jh_j=h_{j+1}U_j$ and $U_jA_j=A_{j+1}U'_j$; the next square is $bi=i'd$. The two end squares use augmentation naturality and the identity laws. A skipped segment crossing the change has $Q$-column $B_lV_{j,l}=V'_{j,l}B_j$; this verifies compatibility with composition, while repetitions give identities. Hence restricting rows commutes with every simplicial operator. Reduction is simplicial by [lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation], with the hammock interpretation of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. Its endpoints are $\gamma_{P',Q}NS$ postcomposed with $d$, and $\gamma_{P',Q'}NT$, respectively.

source.place: Low, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7(ii), printed pp.12-15; agent extension using explicit padded rows, with only weak augmentations.

proof.text: For completeness pass from these explicit simplicial homotopies to the stated homotopy category, meaning simplicial sets localized at weak homotopy equivalences. The projection $r:K\times\Delta^1\to K$ has section $j_0$. The composite $rj_0$ is the identity. On $K\times\Delta^1$ the formula $((z,\theta),\lambda)\mapsto(z,\min(\theta,\lambda))$, with minimum evaluated vertexwise, is a simplicial homotopy from $j_0r$ to the identity: monotone maps remain monotone and restriction commutes with minimum. Together with the constant homotopy on $K$, [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] therefore makes $r$ a weak homotopy equivalence, without a Kan assumption. Both $j_0$ and $j_1$ become its inverse after localization, so the endpoint maps of every map $K\times\Delta^1\to L$ have equal classes. Apply this to $H_a$ postcomposed with $d$ and to $H_b$. Their common endpoint is $\gamma_{P',Q}NS$ postcomposed with $d$. Transitivity gives $[\gamma_{P',Q'}NT]=[d_*c^*\gamma_{P,Q}]$. Concatenation and reduction are the enriched composition of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization], so $d_*c^*$ is exactly the requested action. Only augmentation naturality, two-out-of-three and the stated weak-equivalence components were used; no assertion that $\gamma$ is a weak equivalence has entered.

Step 1: two-out-of-three gives P(alpha), Q(beta) in W. Step 2: the squares hold by the defining equation of I and by augmentation naturality; faces and degeneracies match those of G(-+-) in lem-coef-hammock-graph-colimit-presentation, and reducing into its colimit gives the map into L^H(x,y) of lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization. Step 3: strict naturality for a functor follows from the naturality stated in the graph-colimit node. Step 4: c and d lie in W by two-out-of-three, and T is a functor (I redid the calculation). Steps 5 and 6: I checked every square of the padded rows (+-+- and -+-+) at the 0-to-1 change, including that the internal vertical maps lie in W; skipped segments commute by naturality of a and b. The word category has the injection -+- to +-+-, so the inserted identity column reduces away in the colimit. Step 7: the min-homotopy is simplicial, the cited lem-cbc lemma applies as stated with no Kan or nonemptiness assumption, so the interval projection is a weak equivalence and j0 and j1 agree in the homotopy category; this gives [gamma_{P',Q'} NT] = [d_* c^* gamma_{P,Q}]. Edge cases checked: W equal to identities, c or d equal to 1, empty I, coinciding endpoints, degenerate chains.
